page: Amazon Web Services c6id.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors (Ice Lake 8375C). Operating on the x86_64 architecture at an all-core clock speed of up to 3.5 GHz, this instance features 32 virtual CPUs derived from 16 physical cores via hyperthreading. The configuration is provisioned with 64 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, delivering a dedicated 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio characteristic of compute-intensive infrastructure. In addition, the instance integrates 1,900 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations reveal balanced throughput across raw compute, cryptographic acceleration, and compilation tasks. The instance registered a Geekbench multi-core score of 13,971.0 and a Clang software compilation metric of 26,910.0, benefiting from hardware support for AVX-512 and Vector Neural Network Instructions (VNNI). Memory bandwidth reaches 148.41 GB/s for large uncached block reads and 66.74 GB/s for writes. While small 135M-parameter language model text generation achieves strong efficiency at 308.67 tokens per second, large-scale 70B model inference is constrained by the 64 GB memory capacity, resulting in lower processing throughput of 6.24 tokens per second.

Cost efficiency is achieved by coupling dedicated high-frequency compute threads with dense, direct-attached NVMe storage. Workloads benefit from reduced external EBS input/output operations and minimal latency overhead on temporary files. The primary tradeoff lies in the volatile nature of instance storage and the 2 GB per vCPU allocation, which restricts large in-memory dataset operations. Amazon Web Services c6id.8xlarge is best suited for compute-heavy workloads demanding low-latency temporary disks, such as distributed CI/CD build environments, video encoding, batch processing pipelines, and data transformations.
description: Amazon Web Services c6id.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor and hyperthreaded across 32 vCPUs (16 physical cores). Built on the AWS Nitro System using the x86_64 architecture, the instance includes 64 GB of DDR4 memory, 12 Gbps of baseline networking, and 1,900 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark metrics demonstrate consistent mid-tier execution speeds across general compute routines, reaching a Geekbench multi-core score of 13,971 and a PassMark CPU score of 36,658.6, bolstered by AVX-512 extensions and hardware cryptographic accelerators. The bundled NVMe storage provides significant local I/O throughput without supplemental network storage overhead, making it cost-efficient for transient disk activities. Because system RAM is capped at a 1:2 ratio relative to vCPUs, it is optimized for high-throughput batch processing, compilation workloads, continuous integration, and data transformation routines rather than high-capacity in-memory databases.
